# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

{
  "key": "pr-1289",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running",
    "description": "Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR."
  }
}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. # pr-1289: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running

## Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1289
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1289
- **Title**: fix(1248): dart_tui guard misfires ghost mail-wake turns — log-and-keep-running
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1248-mail-wake-wedge` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +239
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:41:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T13:25:30Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1248.

## Root cause (named)

Not the wake-streak policy and not a wedged await in the messaging fabric. The kill chain was in the vendored dart_tui `Program`:

1. An exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`, or mouse handler hit guards whose failure policy was `enqueue(InterruptMsg())` → `_running = false`: the program died.
2. The embedding CLI kept running its agent loop against the dead controller. `Program.send` silently drops every send to a stopped program (`if (!_running) return;`), and `FaTuiController` never cleared `_running` when `_program.run()` ended — output kept flowing into a void.
3. Net effect on the flake: all 12 wake turns **complete and persist to the session jsonl** (reply to DM #22 is the last session line in every failing run), while the PTY screen never paints the marker. `waitForText` times out 15s later; ESC recovers nothing because the screen is dead, not stalled. The `ps` forensics in the failing runs show the repro process alive at 13-14% CPU for minutes after the wedge — an agent answering into a black hole, which matches the test's own session-tail dump.

The 3 failing SHAs (48d1ffa1f, a2c1a89c9, 31be731cf — all Oct 4) predate today's gh-1197 merge (ae6f9f887), whose `renderGuarded` already defuses the fourth kill path (a throwing `view()` escaping the event loop). That path is now pinned by a regression test; the `InterruptMsg` misfires in the runCmd/update/mouse guards remained live on main and are defused here.

## Delivered

- `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart`: the three exception guards (runCmd, update, mouse handler) log and keep running instead of enqueuing `InterruptMsg`. Only `QuitMsg` and the deliberate `_externalCancellation` interrupt stop the program.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`: `controller.run()` clears `_running` in a `finally` when the program ends — flush timers stop arming into a dead program; pre-run style parks in `_pending` instead of vanishing.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`: `_runTuiRepl` detaches TUI io (`_setTuiIo(null)`, `_tuiController = null`) in a `finally` even when `controller.run()` throws — io can no longer route into a dead controller; a throwing path now degrades to line-mode output (visible) instead of a silent black hole.
- `vendor/dart_tui/test/program_survival_test.dart` (new): pins cmd-throw survival, update-throw survival (both fail-first against the old guards), and the gh-1197 render self-heal.
- `test/integration/dap_wake_hang_test.dart`: wedge forensics now scan the full raw PTY stream for the TUI `Caught … exception` traces (the PTY merges stderr into raw bytes, outside the 600-byte terminal tail window) — next occurrence names the trigger with the right namespace.
- `vendor/dart_tui/CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry documenting the guard-semantics change.

## Quarantine entry (reviewed per the issue)

The issue's requested `scripts/test_quarantine.json` entry is **already on main** and matches the requested JSON exactly (file, test name, issue URL, since 2026-10-04, the 3 run ids). Reviewed as-is; nothing to change. Per gh-1199 AC4 the nightly keeps it supervised for the un-quarantine repeat-run proof — with the fix in, the repeat run should pass and the entry should be dropped.

## Local gate disclosure

Targeted local run (`dart test test/program_survival_test.dart` in the vendor package) was SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137, first attempt, no retry) — the box runs a live LLM loop. Fallback: static review only; this PR's CI is the real gate. No test output is claimed beyond that.

## Remaining

- Un-quarantine repeat-run proof (nightly, gh-1199 AC4) once CI is green on this PR.

Now let me look at the rest of program.dart, particularly the `send` method and `_running` semantics, and how `Program.run` starts and `InterruptMsg` is used. Also check `fa_tui.dart` around the finally and agent_cli_repl_boot.dart.

Key review questions:
1. Guard change: `update()` catch now returns `false` instead of `true`. Previously `enqueue(InterruptMsg()); return true;` — returning true would trigger a re-render of the unchanged model. Now returns false → no re-render. That seems fine since model unchanged.
2. The `InterruptMsg` case in applyMsg still sets `_running = false` — good, external cancellation still works.
3. `runCmd` catch previously also affected `_disableCatchPanics`? Now if `_disableCatchPanics` is true, exceptions are silently swallowed entirely (no log, no interrupt). Was that the case before? Before, when `_disableCatchPanics` was true, InterruptMsg was still enqueued (outside the if). Now with the InterruptMsg removed, with `_disableCatchPanics` true there's no logging and no interrupt — a cmd exception is completely silent. Is `_disableCatchPanics` used anywhere? Let me grep.
4. FaTuiController.run() finally now sets `_running = false`. Need to check what `_send` does with `_pending` when `_running` is false — pre-run style parks in `_pending`. After program ended, `_send` will keep parking messages in `_pending` forever (growing unbounded?) instead of dropping. Check `_send` implementation.
5. agent_cli_repl_boot finally detaches — but does the code after the try/finally rely on `_tuiController`? Check `_runTuiRepl` context.
6. Test file: `_StringSink` — `IOSink` interface in dart:io; they implement it but does IOSink have more members? In current Dart, IOSink has add, write, writeln, writeAll, writeCharCode, addError, addStream, flush, close, done, encoding getter/setter. That seems complete. Also `Utf8Codec` etc — they import dart:io and dart:async; `utf8` and `Encoding` come from dart:io (exported via dart:convert? Actually dart:io exports Encoding and utf8? `utf8` is in dart:convert; dart:io does export dart:convert's Encoding? dart:io exports `Encoding`? IOSink.encoding is of type Encoding, which is from dart:convert, and dart:io re-exports it. `utf8` is defined in dart:convert; does dart:io export it? Hmm — dart:io has `show` exports... Actually `dart:io` does export `utf8`? I believe dart:io exports Encoding but not utf8. Wait — common knowledge: `dart:io` exports `Encoding`, `SystemEncoding`, etc.? Actually `SystemEncoding` is dart:io's. Encoding is defined in dart:convert and dart:io re-exports dart:convert's Encoding? Let me verify: dart:io library declares `export 'dart:convert' show Encoding, ...`? I recall that `dart:io` does export `Encoding`. And `utf8` — in dart:convert. Many programs use `utf8` with only dart:io import and it works because dart:io exports it. Actually yes, dart:io exports `utf8` as part of its API (top-level `Utf8Codec utf8`? no...). Let me just check by running dart analyze or check other vendor tests.

7. Test timing: `_CmdThrowerModel` uses `sequence([...])` — SequenceMsg awaits each runCmd in order. The throwing cmd's exception is caught inside runCmd, then next cmd returns _Survived, then QuitMsg. Fine.

8. In `_ViewThrowerModel`, initial render: renderGuarded(force: true) — view() throws while _throwUntilDisarm is false at first render, so fine. The first frame renders before init cmd runs. Then 'arm' msg processed, needsRender = true (update returns true), renderGuarded throws → renderedOnce is true (first frame succeeded) → self-heal. Then 'disarm', then quit. recovered set when viewsBuilt > 1 without throwing. OK.

Wait — actually there's a subtlety in renderGuarded: after the throw, it enqueues RenderTickMsg only `if (_running && !repeatFailure)`. The re-render on the next real message: 'disarm' arrives → needsRender → render → viewsBuilt++ (not armed now) → recovered = viewsBuilt > 1 → true. Good.

9. Check `withInput(null)` and `withoutRenderer()`, `withoutSignalHandler()` exist as option functions in dart_tui. Grep.

10. Potential issue in fa_tui.dart: setting `_running = false` in finally before restoring termios — but if `run()` is re-entered (controller reused), `_running` set to true again later. Check other uses of `_running` in FaTuiController — e.g. `_send` parking behavior: if `_running` is false and program already ended, parking in `_pending` forever could leak. Look at the code.

11. In agent_cli_repl_boot.dart — check the code after the finally: does anything else reference controller? Also `controller.run()` throwing — the exception propagates up out of `_runTuiRepl`. Where is `_runTuiRepl` called? Does the caller handle? If it throws, what happens — the try/finally detaches io, good, but the exception still propagates. Previously the detach statements would be skipped and exception propagate — same exception behavior, now io detached. Fine.

2. Update guard returns false now vs true before — before it returned true causing re-render of unchanged model; harmless change.

3. The mouse handler guard: `unawaited(runCmd(onMouse(msg)))` — onMouse returns a Cmd; runCmd already catches exceptions from cmd() inside. But note: `runCmd` checks `if (cmd == null || !_running) return;` — good.

4. The `update()` catch writes to stderr unconditionally (not gated on `_disableCatchPanics`). Pre-existing? Before the change it was also unconditional (`stderr.writeln('Caught update exception...')` outside the if). Yes, unchanged behavior.

The bigger design question: removing InterruptMsg from runCmd guard changes semantics for `_disableCatchPanics` mode: when `_disableCatchPanics` is true, cmd exceptions previously still killed the program (InterruptMsg enqueued outside the if block). Now they're fully silent (no log, no death). Check where `_disableCatchPanics` is set/used.

6. Check `Program.send` and `_finished` / kill.
